problem: A tank is being filled with water. The rate of change of the volume of water in the tank $V,$ in milliliters, is directly proportional to the time $t,$ measured in hours. Additionally, the tank is also leaking $200\,\text{ml}$ of water every hour. What is the differential equation that describes the rate of change of the volume of water in the tank, at time $t,$ where $t$ is the time (in hours) since the tank started filling?

html:
Question 3
?

A tank is being filled with water. The rate of change of the volume of water in the tank V, in milliliters, is directly proportional to the time t, measured in hours. Additionally, the tank is also leaking 200ml of water every hour. What is the differential equation that describes the rate of change of the volume of water in the tank, at time t, where t is the time (in hours) since the tank started filling?

a
dVdt=3kt−200,k>0
b
dVdt=kt,k>0
c
dVdt=kt−200,k>0
d
dVdt=k(t−200),k>0
e
dVdt=kt−200,k>0
Submit
